texts.facts: In this case, a Detailed Accident Report (hereinafter referred as DAR) was filed by IO Ombir Singh in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act, which is treated as Claim Petition under Section 166 (1) read with Section 166 (4) MV Act. It pertains to alleged accident of injured Wasim Ahmad (hereinafter referred as claimant), by vehicle bearing Reg. No. HR 55L 9232 (hereinafter referred as offending vehicle), which was driven & owned by Vijender Singh (hereinafter referred as R-1) and insured with Reliance Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd (hereinafter referred as R-2). 2. Preliminary information about the accident was received on 13.04.2017 recorded vide DD no.03 at PS Sun Light Colony. In response to which, ASI Ombir Singh along with Ct. Arun rushed to the spot at NH -24, near Hanuman Mandir (hereinafter referred as spot of accident) where they were informed that injured has already been rushed to hospital. Accidental Taxi bearing Registration No. DL 1RY 4687 and JCB bearing no. HR 55L 9232 were found parked at the spot which were shifted to the police station with the help of crane. Information about MLC of Wasim Ahmad, was received from LNJP wherein he was found admitted but was not in a medical fit state to make statement. Subsequently, on 18.04.2017, he came to police station and his statement with respect to occurrence of accident and his injuries was recorded. He narrated that he was a driver by profession and run vehicle bearing no. DL 1RY 4687 for Meru Cab Company. MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 2 of 35 He stated that his taxi was hit by offending vehicle, a JCB, on Yamuna Bridge, enroute airport from Indirapuram, when it took a sudden U-turn speedily and negligently, thereby his vehicle which caused injuries on his face and right foot. He also revealed the name of JCB driver as Vijender Singh and held him responsible for rash and negligent driving of such JCB Machine causing accident. FIR was registered on the basis of statement of Wasim. Statement u/s 161 Cr.PC was recorded. The accident vehicles were taken into police possession. Relevant documents were collected, result on MLC was also obtained. Driver of offending vehicle was arrested. It was revealed that vehicle was no valid fitness on the date of accident and therefore relevant penal provisions u/s 56/192 MV Act were added. Upon conclusion of investigation, Charge-sheet u/s 279/338 IPC, 56/192 MV Act was filed before Ld. Ilaka MM while DAR was filed in the Tribunal for adjudicating the compensation under Motor Vehicles Act. Proceedings: 3. All the contesting parties appeared before the court. Reply/ WS was filed by both the respondents respectively. In the WS filed on behalf of driver cum owner, it is stated that accident did not take place on account of his rash and negligent driving. He clarified that he was driving the vehicle as Waseem (Dar) vs Vijender (140/17, S.L. Colony) on 24 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143398482/ 2 per the traffic norms but the claimant suddenly came in way of JCB Machine and accident happened. All the other allegations MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 3 of 35 were generally denied. 5. In reply filed by Insurance Company, it is pointed that there is an unexplained delay of 4 days in lodging the FIR. Further, the driver of the taxi was not holding the valid and effective driving license. Further he was not even wearing a seat belt at the time of accident. It is also stated that the vehicle was being plied without fitness which constitute breach of terms of policy in question and therefore liability would solely fall upon the owner of the offending vehicle. It is further submitted that the accident occurred on account of fault and negligence of the taxi driver. It is further submitted that the insurance policy is an Act Only Policy which has not been issued for Third Party. It is accordingly prayed that the R-2 may be exonerated from its liability. Issues: 6. From the pleadings of parties, following issues were framed order dated 09.10.2017: i). Whether the injured Waseem suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 13.04.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing no. HR 55L 9232 driven and owned by R-1 and insured with R-2? OPP. ii). Page No. 4 of 35 same was not led despite repeated opportunities. Interest being accrued to the claimant was also directed to be closed vide order dated 21.03.2018 since the date of framing of issues on 09.10.2017 till the evidence is led. Subsequently, claimant stopped appearing in the matter. The matter was eventually dismissed in default for non appearance as well as for non prosecution vide order dated 24.02.2021. Restoration of case: 8. An application for restoration was filed on 07.02.2023 Waseem (Dar) vs Vijender (140/17, S.L. Colony) on 24 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143398482/ 3 which was allowed vide order dated 09.10.2023 and the matter was restored to its original number and stage. Disability Assessment: 9. Counsel for the claimant filed an application for assessment of physical disability which was allowed and a Disability Assessment Certificate with 03% permanent physical impairment in relation to right foot was received from Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital as noted in the order dated 10.01.2024. Evidence: 10. On 12.02.2024, PW-1 appeared in the witness box and tendered his evidentiary affidavit as Ex.PW1/A and relied upon his medical documents as Ex.PW1/1 (colly) and DAR as Ex.PW1/2. He was put to cross examination by counsel for the R-1 as well as by counsel for R-2. PE was closed upon request vide order dated 13.02.2024. Thereafter, matter was listed for RE which was also closed upon submission made by counsel for R-1 MACT No.: 514/2017 Wasim Ahmad Vs. Vijender & Anr. Page No. 5 of 35 & R-2 respectively that they do not want to lead any evidence as noted in the order dated 20.02.2024. Brief Written Submissions were also filed by counsel for the claimant on the same date.
texts.arguments: As such, it is settled that this issue has to be decided on the scales of preponderance of probabilities and any fishing or roving enquiry is not required to be undertaken into the negligence of the offending vehicle. The aspect of negligence on the part of offending vehicle has already been held into. There is nothing to suggest that taxi driver was running at a very high speed and could not control the vehicle. It appears that he could not decipher and anticipate the sudden turning of JCB which resulted in the collision.
